answer: Since your haze hangs on until midday (and sounds inversion-driven rather than moisture-driven), you actually get a generous window instead of the usual 20-minute fog scramble — I'd shoot from about an hour after sunrise through roughly 11am, with the sweet spot mid-morning when the sun is high enough to glow through the layer but it hasn't started mixing out. Lean into what inversion haze does well: distant, layered subjects like receding ridgelines or buildings that fade into the veil, since nearby contrast stays mostly intact while the far field goes soft and bluish. Meter for the haze rather than letting the camera correct it — give it about a stop of extra exposure on the Tri-X, and on the iPhone shoot ProRAW with HDR off so the phone doesn't "fix" the low contrast you came for.
